name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 35

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: One in the swim accepts a pound to talk nonsense

indicators.note: something that accepts another thing takes it inside itself, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: someone in the swim is a swimmer or bather
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A swimmer lets a pound coin into the pool conversation and starts talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound slips in after the first letter of the bather to make BLATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Blather is a verb meaning to chatter on foolishly at length without saying anything sensible.

clue.text: Internal failure makes mob rising flourish

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads upward, from bottom to top
something internal sits inside, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a loss is a failure or defeat

explanation.surface: A collapse from within lets a crowd uprising thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, rising turns the crowd word upside down; failure then sits in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to come into bloom, and figuratively to develop and thrive, which is what flourish means.

clue.text: Ateam's art moving away from the law actually

indicators.note: the letters are on the move, so they shift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange
in court a question is either one of law or one of fact, so the one away from law is of fact

explanation.surface: A sports team's artistic style is drifting away from the rule book.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawyers separate matters of law from matters of fact; the anagram gives AS A MATTER and the phrase away from law adds OF FACT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to add a surprising truth, meaning in reality or in truth, just as the adverb does.

clue.text: Head off hooligan embrace

indicators.note: with its head off, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a thug is a violent hooligan

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop a yob before he grabs someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letter of THUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A hug is a tight clasp in the arms, the same as an affectionate embrace, as noun or verb.

clue.text: Having got up in time to see war is ending

indicators.note: the answer is there to see in plain view within the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone wakes early enough to witness the end of a war.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides across wa(R IS EN)ding.
explanation.definitionFit: Risen is the past participle of rise, so having risen means having got out of bed or stood up.

clue.text: Condition of some promise

blocks.note: first meaning: a difficult or unfortunate state to be in
second meaning: an old word for a pledge

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about the terms of an undertaking; it is two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a dire predicament, and in older usage also a solemn pledge, surviving in the wedding phrase about troth.

clue.text: Soon to arrive bearing gift?

definitions.note: a punning adverb: in a present-bearing way

blocks.note: first meaning: shortly, in a little while
second meaning, a pun: a present is a gift, so arriving with one is doing it in a present-like manner

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up second sense, splitting the answer as PRESENT plus the adverb ending LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Presently is a standard word for shortly or before long; the pun treats it as the adverb from a present.

clue.text: Murdoch had to start from Dublin maybe

indicators.note: only the start of the word is wanted, its opening letter

blocks.note: Iris Murdoch was a novelist
the opening letter of had

explanation.surface: Iris Murdoch had to begin life in the Irish capital, as indeed she did.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris Murdoch, the novelist and philosopher, was born in Dublin, which makes the surface true.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something originating in Ireland's capital is Irish; maybe flags that Dublin is only one example.

clue.text: Brain in top position at home

definitions.text: Brain in top position at home

blocks.note: surface reading: the brain sits at the top of the body, inside the skull
setter's reading: the person in charge of a household

explanation.walkthrough: Brain stands for the organ the answer's first word names, and the top position at home is the person who runs the household.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the senior member who leads a household, the one with authority over its other members.

clue.text: Selected by Japanese for Korea

blocks.note: first meaning: picked out
second meaning: the name Japan gave Korea during its rule there

explanation.walkthrough: Chosen (Chōsen) was the official Japanese name for Korea from 1910 to 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of choose means picked, and the same spelling is Japan's historical colonial name for the Korean peninsula.

clue.text: Get round the mountains to find some fruit

blocks.note: O is round in shape
mountain ranges are chains of mountains

explanation.surface: A hiker detours around the peaks in search of something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are citrus fruits, so several of them make up some fruit.

clue.text: A few words to be had when one's late

definitions.text: A few words to be had when one's late

blocks.clueFragment: A few words to be had when one's late
blocks.note: surface reading: a quick telling-off waiting for someone who arrives after time
setter's reading: late means dead, and the few words are those carved on a tombstone

explanation.walkthrough: Late looks like unpunctual, but it means deceased, as in the late Mr Smith.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the short inscription or tribute written for a person after death, typically on a gravestone.

clue.text: Not immediately required for soldiers to leave resort

indicators.note: the soldiers are told to go away, so their letters are taken out of the other word

blocks.note: something spare is kept in reserve, not needed now
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops no longer needed are sent off on leave to a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: Take RE from the end of SPARE to leave SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town with mineral springs where people go for health and leisure, a classic resort.

clue.text: Suspense on them is changed on the stroke

indicators.note: the phrase that follows is altered, so its letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tense countdown where something alters exactly as the clock strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom: someone in suspense is said to be on tenterhooks, so the suspense is on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenterhooks were hooks for stretching cloth; being on them is the idiom for anxious waiting and nervous uncertainty.

clue.text: Opera cast upset about nothing

indicators.note: an upset arrangement is knocked out of order, so its letters are reshuffled
the shuffled letters go about, that is around, the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An opera's performers are distressed over a trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast is the anagram fodder, not the singers; its letters are rearranged around the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's famous opera about a singer, her painter lover and the villainous police chief Scarpia.

clue.text: Finishes a game for friends

blocks.note: first meaning: puts the king in checkmate, ending a chess game
second meaning: pals or chums

explanation.surface: Someone wraps up a match so that the pals can go home.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess, to mate the opponent's king ends the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb from checkmate ends a chess game, and the plural noun is everyday British slang for companions.

clue.text: Shabby car check man given a number

blocks.note: the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles
a man is referred to as he
taken as written
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A tatty old car gets inspected by a mechanic who is handed a ticket number.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes eaten by moths are full of holes, so the word describes anything worn, tatty and run-down.

clue.text: Something to drink in New York

definitions.note: the answer is a part of New York, its central borough

blocks.note: first meaning: a whiskey and vermouth cocktail
second meaning: the island borough at the heart of the city

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink while visiting the Big Apple.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocktail of whiskey, sweet vermouth and bitters is named after the island borough that forms central New York City.

clue.text: What the Spanish drink in Scotland?

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A question about what Spanish visitors order at the bar in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a Scottish town is only defined loosely by its location.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a cathedral town in Moray in north-east Scotland, close to many whisky distilleries.

clue.text: No doubt offering willing compliance

blocks.note: first meaning: without question, surely
second meaning: the reply one gives when happily agreeing to a request

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description of an eager helper; the two halves are separate senses of one adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means surely or undoubtedly, and as a standalone reply it signals ready agreement, like 'of course'.

clue.text: Cooks entertaining one of the top people

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: chefs are professional cooks
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Kitchen staff host a dinner for a VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiefs are leaders or heads of organisations, the people at the top of a hierarchy.

clue.text: One takes to the water to engage in the coming rebellion

indicators.note: to engage in something is to be caught up inside it, so the bird sits within the run of words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A recruit joins up for an uprising that is about to break out.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird hides across comin(G REBE)llion.
explanation.definitionFit: A grebe is a diving waterbird of lakes and ponds, so it is something that takes to the water.

clue.text: Qualification raised with first man admitted, it was disclosed

definitions.note: the answer replaces the verb phrase as in 'it emerged that'

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is read upward, from bottom to top
only the first letter of the following word is taken
something admitted is let inside, so this letter goes within the other piece

blocks.note: a degree is an academic qualification
the opening letter of man

explanation.surface: A news report reveals that a degree was upgraded after its first male holder got in.
explanation.walkthrough: DEGREE upside down is EERGED, and M goes in after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: When news emerges it comes out or becomes known, so 'it emerged' says the same as 'it was disclosed'.

clue.text: Creating a pattern of some intelligence

definitions.note: read as the phrase IN FORMATION

blocks.note: first meaning, split into two words
second meaning: news or data, as gathered by spies

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as IN FORMATION for the first sense. Intelligence here is gathered knowledge, not brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the espionage sense means facts and data, which is what the single word means; split, it describes flying in pattern.

clue.text: What's genuine holds good of the Queen

indicators.note: one piece holds the other, keeping it inside

blocks.note: genuine means real
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Whatever is authentic is good enough for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means royal, belonging to or fit for a king or queen, as in her regal bearing.

clue.text: Conclude finer adjustment must be made

indicators.note: the word needs adjusting, so its letters are rearranged into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An engineer decides that a more precise tweak is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or reason from evidence to a judgment, which is what conclude means as a verb.

clue.text: Time to get through half the business

indicators.note: only half of the word that follows is kept, the first three of its six letters

blocks.note: a business such as a travel firm is an agency

explanation.surface: Someone needs time to work through a share of the firm's workload.
explanation.walkthrough: Business gives AGENCY, and its first half is AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is a long period or era, so the word stands for time, as in 'it took an age'.

clue.text: Anxious to give the priest anything

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, title of a Catholic priest
aught is an old word for anything at all

explanation.surface: A worried parishioner frets about having nothing to offer the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraught describes a tense, stressed person or situation, full of worry and nervous strain.

clue.text: Anticipating trouble if range has to be adjusted

indicators.note: the words need adjusting, so their letters are moved into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A marksman worries the shots will go astray unless the sights are reset.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear something is to dread it in advance, so the participle means expecting something bad to happen.

clue.text: That's everything finished!

blocks.note: first meaning: the whole lot
second meaning: used up or over

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper announces that the stock has completely sold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's all' can mean that's the lot, and all on its own is a regional word for used up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the whole amount, and in northern English and American dialect it also means used up or gone.

clue.text: Taken by boy who has found a way round

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
O is round in shape
Len is a boy's name, short for Leonard

explanation.surface: A lad has been led off by a young lad who knows a detour.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the order way, round, boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen means taken without permission, the past participle of steal, which matches the passive sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Sent university back into debt

indicators.note: going back means the university name is read from right to left
one piece is put into the other, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: Yale is an American Ivy League university
being in debt is being in the red

explanation.surface: A graduate is sent home owing money to the college.
explanation.walkthrough: Being in debt is being in the red, a convention from red ink in ledgers; the reversed university goes between its R and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay a message is to pass it on, so relayed means sent onward or transmitted.
